chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, he said:
I asked him about salat (prayer) in the skins of foxes, and he said: If they have been properly slaughtered, then there is no harm.

key_terms.الثَّعَالِبِ: foxes, the specific animal mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship being discussed
key_terms.جُلُودِ: skins or hides used as garments or coverings
key_terms.ذَكِيَّةً: properly slaughtered according to Islamic law
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) wearing fox skins if they are properly slaughtered?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat (prayer) in fox skins. It states that if the skins are from animals that are properly slaughtered, then there is no problem in praying in them.
